{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# Submit with (translated from Slurm):
#   flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 10 -g 1 -t 5d \
#     -o output=3sl.out \
#     bash ./3sl.flux.sh
#
# NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=10240 not translated.
# Performance implication: without a per-core memory reservation/limit, the job may be scheduled onto nodes without sufficient free memory per core, increasing the risk of memory pressure or OOM kills and potentially reducing performance.
#
# NOTE: Slurm -J 3sl not translated.
# Performance/ops implication: job naming/identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.
#
# NOTE: Slurm --export=ALL not translated.
# Performance implication: usually none (Flux typically runs with the current environment), but if your site sanitizes environments, missing exports could change runtime behavior.

module load anaconda
conda activate ilab
export PYTHONPATH="/adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/tensorflow-caney"

# Slurm used: srun -G1 -n1 python ...
# Flux equivalent: run within the allocation granted by `flux batch`.
flux run -n 1 -c 10 -g 1 \
  python /adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/senegal-lcluc-tensorflow/projects/land_cover/scripts/predict.py \
    -c /adapt/nobackup/people/jacaraba/development/senegal-lcluc-tensorflow/projects/land_cover/configs/20220620/land_cover_256_trees_srv.yaml
"
}
